reconstruction.scope: Specific standing Apollo sanctuary at Pompeii: roofless raised podium/cella with two tall fluted front columns and varied broken stumps, frontal pale/brick stair, separate pale altar with rolled ends and sundial column; surrounding open court has surviving/broken fluted portico shafts and a short east entablature, rough enclosing walls and an original simplified volumetric bronze replica figure. No restored temple roof/pediment, broad precinct slab or copied sculpture/text atlas.

reconstruction.heightBasis: Picture/map estimates only: central podium12.5x22m with its upper floor2.4m above anchor DEM datum; roofless cella6.8x12.8m, surviving walls1.4-2.6m above podium, front columns6.3m above podium and varied0.6-1.8m stumps. Frontal stair6m wide with16steps. Court side rows12 stations each and end rows5 intermediate stations each: original simplified approximate survival inventory, not an archaeological survey. Short east four-column entablature about4.6m above local floor. Altar2.8x1.55m, sundial4.7m high, replica figure1.75m. Hidden wall/column inventories and precise capital/repair details approximate.
reconstruction.terrainBasis: Original standard6m Mapzen ground, native paths, water and independent buildings retained. Only the occupied temple podium, short stair, altar footing and narrow column/wall footings are authored. Open court/portico floors remain native ground. Grade-following peripheral bases and buried occupied foundations; no broad precinct slab, flattening or ground/water cutout. Coarse DEM cannot resolve level excavated paving, precise step/threshold or absolute archaeological floor levels.
